model: REIT AFFO capitalization at cost of equity (hand-built, non-engine route)

inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted, FY2025 10-K basis (SEC XBRL); modest buybacks ($1.6B remaining authorization) roughly offset ongoing equity issuance/SBC dilution, held flat as a simplifying base-case assumption
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2025-12-31 (FY2025 10-K); Q2 2026 10-Q shows total debt $37,189.6M, cash $1,762.5M, shares 466.265M -- close to FY2025 anchors, FY2025 year-end used for consistency with the AFFO capitalization base
inputs.wacc_rationale: Not a WACC -- AFFO is a post-interest, post-financing-cost cash flow, so it is capitalized at the COST OF EQUITY, not WACC, and net debt is never subtracted from the resulting equity value (that would double-count leverage already embedded in AFFO). Cost of equity built from ~4.3% 10yr UST + an equity risk premium reflecting AMT's leverage (~$37B debt), REIT rate sensitivity (flagged high in the qualitative analysis), and EM (LatAm/Africa) currency and counterparty exposure: base 9.5%, bull 8.75% (rate relief / re-rating), bear 10.5% (rate shock, EM stress, DISH contagion).
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable -- AMT is the LESSOR on towers (ground leases to carriers are the revenue-generating asset), and AFFO is management's own post-maintenance-capex, post-straight-line, post-non-cash-item cash flow measure; no separate lease adjustment layered on top.
inputs.nci_treatment: Not separately stripped -- FY2025 net income and AFFO guidance are management's consolidated figures net of the (immaterial for AMT) minority interests in certain international JVs; not material enough to warrant a separate NCI leakage adjustment.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: AMT is a REIT (tower/data-center real estate, IAS-style fair-value-adjacent GAAP conventions, externally-facing distribution policy) per the dcf-methods routing table -- an owner-FCF DCF would double-count leverage (AFFO is already post-interest) and would be distorted by non-cash straight-line rent and heavy D&A on tower assets. Used AFFO-per-share capitalization at the cost of equity instead, anchored on management's own FY2026 guidance of ~$11.08 AFFO/share (Q2 2026 earnings, second guidance raise of the year) rather than a from-scratch owner-FCF build. DATA QUALITY WARNING: the Revenue/RevenueContinuing columns in AMT_Metrics.csv and core_metrics are UNRELIABLE from FY2019 onward -- annual Revenue prints $495-936M (a small fraction of AMT's actual ~$10-11B revenue), and quarterly revenue values are inconsistent across periods (some quarters show ~$2.5B, correct in isolation, others ~$100-250M, evidently a single revenue sub-line mistagged by the XBRL extraction, likely coinciding with the ASC 842 lease-accounting transition and/or a non-consolidated revenue concept). OperatingIncome, NetIncome, OperatingCashFlow, CapEx, TotalDebt, CashAndEquivalents, SharesOutstanding and DividendPerShare all cross-check cleanly against AMT's known public financial history and were used as anchors; Revenue was NOT used for this valuation. This should be corrected in the underlying XBRL extraction (scripts/build_facts_xbrl.py) on a future refresh -- flagged here rather than fixed, per this agent's scope (no scripts/ edits). AFFO itself is a non-GAAP measure AMT discloses in its earnings release/presentation prose, not a tagged XBRL concept, so no historical AFFO series exists in core_metrics; the base-year AFFO/share of $11.08 is sourced from the qualitative Analysis JSON's guidance section (Q2 2026 earnings, Aug 2026), itself sourced from AMT's own investor materials.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management's own AFFO/share growth framework (Q2 2026 guidance: ~3% contractual escalators + 2-3% new business, plus CoreSite mix lift), not a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue CAGR fields are null because the Revenue column in AMT_Metrics.csv is corrupted from FY2019 onward (see inputs.notes) and was excluded rather than used to compute a misleading CAGR. EPS and FCF CAGRs are also distorted by one-off items (FY2022-23 EPS depressed by LatAm/impairment charges and share-count dilution from the CoreSite-era capital raises; FY2019-20 FCF base reflects the pre-CoreSite, pre-India-exit portfolio) and are shown for reference only -- they were NOT used to set the AFFO growth path, which instead follows management's own guided framework.

base.narrative: FY2026 AFFO/share = management's own guidance ($11.08, raised twice in 2026). Growth accelerates from the guided 2026 'trough' (DISH churn fully anniversaries, Sprint decommissioning substantially winds down) toward management's long-term organic framework of ~3% escalators + 2-3% new business, lifted further by CoreSite's faster (~15%, moderating to high-single-digit) growth as it scales, then fades to a 4.0% terminal-approach rate reflecting a mature, still-inflation-linked but slower-growing portfolio. Terminal growth of 3.2% sits above US CPI-linked escalators alone to reflect the CoreSite/data-center mix shift, but below the near-term double-digit CoreSite growth rate, which cannot persist as CoreSite scales against land-constrained facilities.

bull.narrative: DISH/Latin America drags resolve faster than guided (WOM/AT&T Mexico disputes settle, no further tenant defaults), CoreSite's AI-driven demand surge persists longer and at a larger scale (development pipeline triples capacity as guided), and a benign rate environment both lowers the cost of equity and supports multiple re-rating across tower REITs. Slightly higher 2026 AFFO/share base (less severe near-term drag) than the base case.

bear.narrative: DISH/EchoStar bankruptcy proceedings spread further tower revenue at risk beyond the initial ~$200M annualized hit (170+ industry lawsuits create an overhang), Latin America weakness persists past 2027 (WOM, AT&T Mexico, further currency devaluation), carrier consolidation reduces colocation demand, and a rate shock (long-term Treasury yields rise materially) both raises AMT's cost of equity and its refinancing costs given ~$37B of debt. CoreSite growth decelerates sharply if AI infrastructure capex cools. Lower 2026 AFFO/share base reflects a deeper near-term drag than guided.

scenario_narratives.base: AFFO/share grows from the guided FY2026 trough of $11.08 as DISH and Sprint churn anniversary through 2026-2027, reaccelerating toward management's long-term ~5-8% framework (escalators + new business + CoreSite mix), then fading to a 4% approach rate. Discounted at a 9.5% cost of equity (reflecting AMT's leverage and rate sensitivity) with a 3.2% terminal growth capitalization.
scenario_narratives.bull: DISH/LatAm headwinds resolve faster, CoreSite's AI-driven leasing surge persists at scale, and a friendlier rate backdrop both lowers the cost of equity and lifts the sector multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: DISH bankruptcy litigation spreads further tower revenue at risk, Latin America stays weak past 2027, carrier consolidation slows new colocation demand, and a rate shock raises AMT's cost of equity and refinancing costs against its ~$37B debt load.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 25/50/25. AMT is an investment-grade, contractually-escalated tower REIT with a well-telegraphed near-term drag (DISH, Latin America) that management has already quantified and guided through twice in 2026 -- the base case is not speculative, it is management's own raised guidance extrapolated on its own stated growth framework. Bear case captures genuine rate and EM-counterparty tail risk (flagged 'high' and 'moderate-to-high' in the qualitative risk analysis) rather than a remote scenario, so it is not underweighted below the house default.

valuation_philosophy.summary: AMT is valued as a REIT: AFFO per share (management's own non-GAAP cash-generation measure, already net of interest expense, maintenance capex and non-cash items) is projected forward and capitalized at the cost of equity -- never at a blended WACC, and net debt is never subtracted from the resulting equity value, since AFFO already reflects the cost of AMT's ~$37B of debt. The base case starts from management's own twice-raised FY2026 AFFO/share guidance of $11.08 and grows it along management's own stated long-term organic framework (escalators + new business + CoreSite mix), tapering to a terminal growth rate anchored to CPI-linked escalators plus a moderating data-center growth contribution. The resulting weighted intrinsic value of ~$214/share sits close to the Street's own ~$215 average analyst price target cited in the qualitative research, an external cross-check rather than a coincidence, since both anchor on the same guided AFFO trajectory.
key_risks_to_valuation: AMT's Revenue and RevenueContinuing figures in the underlying Metrics.csv/core_metrics are corrupted from FY2019 onward (see inputs.notes) -- this valuation deliberately does not use them, but a future refresh of this ticker should not trust them either until the XBRL extraction is fixed

AFFO/share is a non-GAAP measure defined by AMT itself and is not independently auditable the way GAAP revenue or net income are; a change in AMT's own AFFO definition would break comparability of this model's historical anchor
DISH/EchoStar bankruptcy litigation (170+ lawsuits) could strip materially more than the ~$200M already removed from the run-rate if courts side with tenants on lease decommissioning terms
Latin America (WOM, AT&T Mexico arbitration) is guided to stay weak through 2027; a base case that is too optimistic on the pace of LatAm stabilization overstates AFFO growth in years 2-3

High leverage (~$37B debt) makes both AMT's actual cost of equity and its refinancing costs unusually sensitive to long-term Treasury yields; a sustained rate shock could compress the model materially beyond the bear case shown here

CoreSite's AI-driven growth is the single largest swing factor between bull and base cases and depends on the durability of hyperscaler/AI capital spending, which this qualitative research flags as a moderate risk

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 160.06-196.08
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL via research/AMT/Reports/AMT.duckdb core_metrics (OperatingIncome, NetIncome, OperatingCashFlow, CapEx, TotalDebt, CashAndEquivalents, SharesOutstanding, DividendPerShare, StockBasedComp cross-checked against public record; Revenue/RevenueContinuing columns excluded as unreliable, see inputs.notes)
data_sources.qualitative: research/AMT/Reports/AMT_Analysis.json (2026-09-25), sourced from Q2 2026 earnings release/call (August 2026) for guidance figures and DISH/LatAm/CoreSite developments

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
